reasons: The script does not check the status code before reading results in the step-by-step version.
It publishes real surveys when validation passes.

terms.meaning: The full chain of steps from plan to publish, run by one request.
An outside survey platform where the finished survey is hosted.
A number showing how ready a survey is, from the validation checks.
The computer the script is running on.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Server address and imports
sections.what: Brings in the tools for sending web requests and handling JSON, and sets the server address to the local machine on port 8000.
sections.why: Likely reason: the example talks to a server running on this computer.
sections.watch_out: The server must be running before the script starts.

sections.name: create_b2b_csat_survey (part 1)
sections.title: Describe goal and send workflow request
sections.what: Builds the research brief, including goal, audience, markets, size, length, required items, language, platform and context. Sends it to the full workflow address and stops if the server reports an error.
sections.why: Likely reason: one request runs the whole pipeline.
sections.watch_out: A successful run may publish a real survey to Qualtrics when validation passes.

sections.name: create_b2b_csat_survey (part 2)
sections.title: Show results and save file
sections.what: Prints the survey ID, status, readiness score, section list, sample questions, issues and link. Saves the full result as a JSON file in the current folder.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a short readable summary and a complete record.
sections.watch_out: The file is written to the current folder and overwrites any file with the same name.

sections.name: create_step_by_step (part 1)
sections.title: Plan and author in separate calls
sections.what: Runs planning and then authoring as separate calls, and prints the section and question counts.
sections.why: The docstring says this is for more control over each step.
sections.watch_out: The planning route is not visible in the sections shown, so confirm it exists on the server.

sections.name: create_step_by_step (part 2)
sections.title: Validate and publish separately
sections.what: Runs validation, then publishes to Qualtrics with a fixed name only if validation passed. Prints the survey link.
sections.why: Likely reason: a survey with failing checks should not be published.
sections.watch_out: Publishing creates a real survey. Repeated runs may create several surveys with the same name, and the status code is not checked.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Choose which example runs
sections.what: When the file runs directly, it calls only the full workflow example. The step-by-step example is commented out.
sections.why: The comment says the full workflow is the recommended path.
sections.watch_out: Running the file starts a real workflow that may publish a survey.

summary: A runnable script that asks the local server to build a complete B2B customer satisfaction survey and prints a readable summary.
purpose: Shows a user how to call the full workflow and what the results look like.
why: Likely reason: a working example is the fastest way to learn the system.
how: Builds a research brief, sends it to the workflow address, prints the survey structure, sample questions, validation issues and link, then saves the full result to a JSON file. A second function does the same work in separate steps.
inputs: A research brief written in the script, and a server running at the local address.
outputs: Printed summary text and a file named b2b_csat_result.json in the folder the script runs from.
risks: A successful run can publish a real survey to Qualtrics. The saved file overwrites any file with the same name. Field names must match the server.
debug: If the server is not reachable, start it and check the address. If a key error appears, compare the response with the fields the script reads. If the step-by-step version fails, check the planning address.
